definition.title: Bright Babies
definition.description:
Please count ALL family members who will be attending when registering.

The expectation is to try to attend all 4 sessions.

Bright Babies is a 4-part workshop and storytime for babies and their parents/caregivers designed to model ways to read, talk, sing, and play with children ages 0-18 months. Through modelling, sharing early literacy tips, small group activities, and discussions, the sessions will provide information on early literacy practices for parents and caregivers to help them support their children’s early language and literacy development. The enhanced storytimes will include a component focused on parent/caregiver education as it relates to early learning development and parent-child well-being to promote parent-child bonding and to ameliorate the effects of toxic stress on young children.

definition.title: Learning Together:  Discover Ways to Help Your Child Learn
definition.description:
This 5-week family literacy program helps parents and children, aged 2.5 to 5, build a love of reading together and improve literacy skills using the alphabet, numbers, stories and active play.

The program is designed for caregiver and child to participate together. All materials and resources will be provided.

Topics include:

· Reading & Writing - November 1

· Early Math - November 8

· Speech Development - November 15

· Screen Time & Technology - November 22

· Rhythm & Movement - November 29

Please register for each week individually. Please register each child aged 2-5 individually (siblings are welcome, however childminding is only available to children ages 2-5). Drop-ins welcome as space allows.

Sponsored by the Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills. Presented in partnership with Literacy Richmond.

definition.title: Learning Together:  Discover Ways to Help Your Child Learn
definition.description:
This 5-week family literacy program helps parents and children, aged 2.5 to 5, build a love of reading together and improve literacy skills using the alphabet, numbers, stories and active play.

The program is designed for caregiver and child to participate together. All materials and resources will be provided.

Topics include:

· Reading & Writing - November 1

· Early Math - November 8

· Speech Development - November 15

· Screen Time & Technology - November 22

· Rhythm & Movement - November 29

Please register for each week individually. Please register each child aged 2-5 individually (siblings are welcome, however childminding is only available to children ages 2-5). Drop-ins welcome as space allows.

Sponsored by the Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills. Presented in partnership with Literacy Richmond.
